benchmark: AstraDJ local multi-room Lounge acceptance and performance

runtime.frontendMode: Vite development server; real production bundles and deployment infrastructure are not used.

methodology.queueWorkload: 3 rooms concurrently; 50 authenticated participants per room; 1 queue additions per second per room for 30 seconds; operations start at configured intervals and are flushed before report. Room lg_a105353b598d0eed uses 50 real Chromium/React clients; other rooms use authenticated Socket.IO clients.
methodology.warmup: No synthetic mutation warm-up is included; join and schema index initialization occur before measurement.
methodology.trace: Each queue addition carries a UUID correlation ID through the server receipt, durable QueueEvent, broadcast, browser Socket.IO handler, React state commit, and DOM marker. Browser event-receipt and state-commit hooks use performance.timeOrigin + performance.now(); DOM completion is timestamped after the React commit and two requestAnimationFrame callbacks. The correlation UUID is enabled only for the benchmark and does not bypass authentication, membership, or rate limits.
methodology.queueDriftDefinition: Per mutation: server queue-command receipt (gateway Date.now timestamp) to the last of all 50 measured browser clients completing the correlated DOM marker and matching the expected current/up-next track IDs. This is the PRD mutation-to-all-clients delay; browser render spread and receipt-to-render are reported separately.
methodology.clockMethod: All API processes, Vite, Chromium pages, and Socket.IO clients run on this one Windows host. Inter-process measurements compare Unix-epoch timestamps from Date.now and browser performance.timeOrigin + performance.now on the same host clock, with a stated 1 ms resolution allowance. No timestamps from unsynchronized remote hosts are subtracted; browser and host clock offset has not been validated on another machine.
methodology.rateLimitHandling: The benchmark uses a unique disposable database. To collect more than five segue samples per room despite the production limit of 10 playback actions/user/minute, the benchmark clears only the disposable database rate-limit counters before segue sample 16. Rate-limit throughput is not measured by this workload.
methodology.clientApplyAndRender: For the measured browser room, record server receipt, browser event receipt, React state application in useLayoutEffect, and DOM track IDs after two animation frames. Socket.IO driver clients in the other rooms retain the setImmediate callback proxy for separate, non-PRD UI evidence.
methodology.percentiles: Nearest-rank p50/p95/p99 (ceil(p*n), 1-based); per-metric sample count shown. Browser queue metric has 5 complete event samples of 30 requested and 50 DOM clients per sample; server/fan-out metrics cover 73 accepted events of 90 attempts across all rooms.
methodology.chatAndReconnect: One unique persisted chat message per room delivered to every currently joined socket; disconnect a listener, send a second message, reconnect/join, and verify authoritative queue snapshot plus history recovery.
methodology.clientSourceAddresses: Each room uses a distinct loopback source address (127.0.0.1 onward) so its 50 initial sockets remain below the shared per-IP connection-attempt limit; this does not model a single-NAT multi-room burst.
methodology.lifecycle: Host end command, durable ended status, and end notification count observed in the Socket.IO rooms; lifecycle and chat/reconnect checks are reported as skipped for the browser-measured room.
methodology.browserAuth: Each browser client uses an isolated context and a refresh-token cookie seeded only in the disposable Mongo database; the application restores a distinct real user session and Socket.IO authenticates normally. Contexts are opened sequentially to avoid startup bursts; all pages share one local Chromium process. Browser pages connect through Vite to the first API process; both API instances share the same Mongo database.

prdTargets.concurrentRoomDescription: handful; local acceptance uses the configured room count

queueSyncDrift.boundary: Server queue-mutation handler receipt to the last of 50 real React queue DOM render markers; two requestAnimationFrame callbacks follow React commit. One local room only.

webSocketFanout.boundary: Server handler receipt to final Socket.IO client receipt on one host.

chatAndReconnect.reason: Chat/reconnect coverage runs through the Socket.IO cohorts in the other concurrent rooms.

segue.disposition: Service/socket proxy only; no real media clock or browser render measurement. P95 target remains unverified even if the proxy is below 3000 ms.

lifecycle.reason: Host lifecycle coverage runs through the Socket.IO cohorts in the other concurrent rooms.

prdDisposition.queueSyncDrift: Local actual browser/React DOM measurement for 50 clients in one room; other rooms use Socket.IO-only clients. Not production-representative.
prdDisposition.webSocketFanout: Estimated from instrumented server receipt and envelope broadcast time plus per-client clock offset correction; local shared-host clock. Production network fan-out remains unverified.
prdDisposition.roomCapacity: Exercised at PRD design capacity in each local room; not production capacity proof.
prdDisposition.multipleRooms: 3 rooms exercised concurrently across two app processes against one local MongoDB instance.
prdDisposition.segue: Measured separately from queue event fan-out and remains unverified at the true outro-entry-to-browser-rendered boundary.
